title: Proteomic analysis of murine small intestinal epithelial cells pre-and postweaning
projectDescription: Characterization of the global, organ-and site-specific as well as single-cell transcriptional and proteomic profile of the small intestinal epithelium at different time points after birth. The proteomic analysis was performed on total isolated small intestinal epithelium from 1-,5-,1-0 and 25-day-old mice.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Each sample corresponded to one given animal, except for day 1 samples for which the small intestine of three 1-day-old animals were pooled. Samples were lysed in 150 µL lysis buffer (4% SDS, 100 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 100 mM DTT) and heated for 5 min at 95°C. Samples were sonicated for 10 s, centrifuged at 16,000g and added onto 10 kDa cutoff filters (#ODC010C33, PALL). Protein concentrations were measured at 280 nm using Nanodrop (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and samples alkylated and digested using the filter-aided sample preparation method (Wisniewskiet.al. 2009). Peptide concentration after elution was measured at 280 nm using Nanodrop and peptides cleaned on StageTip C18 columns (Rappsilber et.al. 2007) prior to mass-spectrometry (MS) analysis. NanoLC-MS/MS was performed on an EASY-nLC 1000 system (ThermoFisher), connected to a QExactive Mass Spectrometer (ThermoFisher) via a nanoelectrospray ion source.
dataProcessingProtocol: MS raw files were processed with MaxQuant software version 1.5.7.4 (Cox and Mann, 2008)and peak lists were identified by searching against the mouse UniProt protein database (downloaded 2018.07.11). Searches were performed using trypsin as an enzyme, maximum 2 missed cleavages, precursor tolerance of 20 ppm in the first search used for recalibration, followed by 7 ppm for the main search and 0.5 Da for fragment ions. Carbamidomethylation of cysetine was set as a fixed modification, methionine oxidation and protein N-terminal acetylation were set as variable modifications. The required false discovery rate (FDR) was set to 1% both for peptide and protein levels and the minimum required peptide length was set to seven amino acids. Label free quantification (LFQ) based on two peptides was used.
